user_goal: Configure a sticker-like product to sell in packs, entering the price of one pack rather than a per-piece price, and see the shopping-feed URL to hand to the ad channels.
business_goal: Let staff price consumables the way they actually sell them (per pack) without changing the per-unit wire contract the pricing engine, bulk discounts and API clients all depend on.

user_journey.step: Sign in to the admin panel
Open the Products list and note the shopping feed URL card
Open a sticker-like product for editing
Set the pack size and unit label, review the tier table in pack mode
Save and confirm the per-unit wire values the backend stored
Open an order containing a pack product

happy_path.action: Log in as the seeded super admin
happy_path.expected_result: Lands on the admin dashboard with an in-memory access token (never localStorage).

happy_path.action: Open /products and read the Shopping feed card
happy_path.expected_result: A read-only card shows NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL + '/feeds/products.xml' with a copy button and a note naming the three channels; no new backend call is made for it.

happy_path.action: Open Custom Die-Cut Stickers for editing and expand Pricing Tiers
happy_path.expected_result: Pack controls render at the top of the section: label 'Sold in packs of', #pack-size-input (default 1) and the unit-label input (default 'pcs'); the table header reads 'Quantity' / 'Price / unit (₹)' / 'MRP / unit (₹)' while pack size is 1.

happy_path.action: Set the pack size to 50 and leave the unit label as 'pcs'
happy_path.expected_result: Table switches to pack mode: headers become 'Packs' / 'Price per pack (₹)' / 'MRP per pack (₹)'. Existing tiers rehydrate from the stored per-unit values, e.g. 50 pcs @ ₹15.00/unit becomes 1 pack @ ₹750.00, 250 pcs @ ₹6.00/unit becomes 5 packs @ ₹1500.00. Each row shows '= N pcs' (data-testid 'tier-pieces') and '₹X.XX/pc' (data-testid 'tier-per-piece').

happy_path.action: Enter 300 as the price per pack on the 1-pack row and read the per-piece readout
happy_path.selector: input aria-label 'Price per pack for pricing tier 1'; p[data-testid='tier-per-piece']
happy_path.expected_result: Accepted with no field error; the per-piece line reads '₹6.00/pc' because 30000 paise divides evenly by 50, and the hidden wire value price_per_unit becomes 6.00.

happy_path.action: Save the product and re-read it from the admin API
happy_path.expected_result: 200. Stored pack_size=50, unit_label='pcs', and tier quantities unchanged in pieces with price_per_unit stored per unit (6.00 for the edited row). pricing_updated_at is not bumped by a pack-only change.

happy_path.action: Return to /products and read the pack product's lowest-tier price cell
happy_path.expected_result: The cell shows the price per pack for the pack product; sorting stays per-piece per spec decision D5.

happy_path.action: Open an order that contains a pack product and read the item quantity
happy_path.expected_result: Quantity renders as 'N packs (M pcs)' from the order item's snapshotted pack_size/unit_label, which orders.ts reads in either snake or camel case and defaults to 1/'pcs'.

alternate_paths.path_name: Pack size back to 1 restores per-unit entry

steps.action: Set the pack size from 50 back to 1 without saving
steps.expected_result: Table headers revert to 'Quantity' / 'Price / unit (₹)' / 'MRP / unit (₹)' and the same stored wire tiers are re-expressed per unit with no numeric drift.

steps.action: On a pack product with MRP, read the MRP per pack column
steps.selector: input aria-label 'MRP per pack for pricing tier 1'
steps.expected_result: MRP hydrates as mrp_per_unit x pack_size (e.g. ₹12.00/unit at pack 50 shows ₹600.00) and the Discount preview percentage is unchanged, since percent off is scale-invariant.

steps.action: Search the Print Specs section for a Quantity steps editor
steps.expected_result: No quantity-steps editor is rendered and the field is never sent, so a PATCH leaves the stored value untouched (spec decision D6).

error_paths.trigger: Enter 100 as the price per pack while pack size is 30
error_paths.expected_ui_response: Inline field error under 'Price per pack': '₹100 per pack does not divide into whole paise per piece at pack size 30' (zod superRefine on the pack_price path, integer-paise check, never float division).
error_paths.selector: input aria-label 'Price per pack for pricing tier 1' + sibling error paragraph

error_paths.trigger: Set pack size to 30 while the product's stored tier quantities are 50/100/250/500/1000
error_paths.expected_ui_response: Save is rejected and the backend's 422 pack_size_tier_mismatch message is surfaced on the pack_size field: 'Every pricing tier quantity must be a multiple of the pack size. Change the pack size or the tier quantities.'

error_paths.trigger: Give two options in the same group the same label ignoring case and punctuation, e.g. finishes 'Matte Lamination' and 'matte-lamination'
error_paths.expected_ui_response: Client-side zod flags only the later duplicate row with DUPLICATE_OPTION_MESSAGE on finishes.<i>.label; a backend 422 duplicate_option_label is routed to the same group via optionGroupFromMessage, which matches an anchored prefix so a quoted label containing another group's name cannot mis-target the section.
error_paths.selector: PrintSpecsSection row error (role='alert'); optionGroupFromMessage in src/lib/api/validationErrors.ts

error_paths.trigger: Enter a pack size of 0 or above 1,000,000
error_paths.expected_ui_response: Inline pack-size error from the zod bounds (1..1,000,000); the input itself carries min=1 and max=PACK_SIZE_MAX.

error_paths.trigger: Enter a unit label that fails the regex, e.g. '123' or a leading symbol
error_paths.expected_ui_response: Inline unit-label error; the stored label must match ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9 ./-]{0,29}$ and is kept as typed, not lowercased.
error_paths.selector: input aria-label 'Unit label' + pack-section error paragraph

edge_cases.case: A stored tier quantity is not divisible by the pack size when the form hydrates
edge_cases.existing_validation: wireTierToPack / hydrateTiers show the row in an error state rather than crashing (spec section 7)
edge_cases.risk_note: Silently rounding here would change a live price; the row must surface the problem and leave the stored value alone until staff fix it.

edge_cases.case: Pack-mode inputs are form-only and could be stripped by zod
edge_cases.existing_validation: packs / pack_price / pack_mrp are declared in tierSchema precisely so z.object does not strip them, and the wire values are re-derived in both a PricingSection effect and buildProductPayload
edge_cases.risk_note: A dropped key would silently erase the tier's price on a PATCH, which replaces the whole tier list.

edge_cases.case: An option multiplier makes the pack price non-exact
edge_cases.existing_validation: optionRoundingNotes renders a non-blocking role='status' hint (data-testid 'pack-rounding-note')
edge_cases.risk_note: This must stay advisory: the charge is always rounded_unit x quantity, so the hint explains a real rounding, it is not a validation failure.

edge_cases.case: Pack size changed on a product that already has conforming tiers
edge_cases.existing_validation: Route validates the merged state (sent fields plus existing values), not just the payload
edge_cases.risk_note: A PATCH may carry pack_size without tiers or tiers without pack_size; validating only the payload would let a mismatch through.

edge_cases.case: Admin access token is in-memory only
edge_cases.existing_validation: authStore keeps the token out of localStorage; _hasHydrated gates AuthGuard
edge_cases.risk_note: A Lighthouse final_state checkpoint taken after login gets bounced to /login, so lighthouse must stay off for these steps (pipeline README, known per-app wrinkles).

gaps: The feed URL card is derived entirely from NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL with no backend call, so the admin cannot tell from this screen whether the feed route is actually serving. Locally it is not: resolve_link_base rejects a localhost FRONTEND_URL and the route returns 503 feed_not_configured, and the card gives no hint of that.
Bulk discount remains per-piece: the preview payload carries no pack_size, so a pack product's bulk discount is still entered and previewed per unit.
No admin surface exercises invalid_pack_multiple (it is a cart/order code); it is mapped in validationErrors.ts but unreachable from the admin UI.
